blocks.text: Table of Contents
1. System Architecture & Concepts
This chapter explains the foundational concepts that apply across the entire application. Understanding these makes every module easier to use.
1.1 Multi-Tenancy
SITHEHR supports multiple hospitals running on the same installation. Each hospital is a Tenant with a unique tenant_id that matches hospitals.id in the database. The DEMO hospital is tenant_id = 1.
How it works in practice:

items: Every tenant-scoped model uses the ScopedByTenant trait. This trait automatically adds a WHERE tenant_id = ? clause to every query, where the tenant_id comes from request()->attributes->get('tenant_id').
The tenant_id is set on the request when a user logs in - it reflects the hospital the user belongs to.
Master data (departments, provinces, cities, barangays, genders, etc.) is tenant-scoped. When you create a department, it is created for YOUR hospital only. Other hospitals do not see it.
To access data across tenants (e.g. in reports or administrative queries), the code explicitly uses withoutGlobalScopes() and re-adds the tenant filter manually.
When you see a dropdown that appears empty, check: (1) Is the master data created for YOUR tenant? (2) Are you logged in as the correct hospital's user?

blocks.text: 1.2 Soft Deletes and History
SITHEHR does not physically delete records. Instead, it uses a soft-delete pattern with a history column:

items: history = 1: the record is current/active and visible in normal queries.
history = 0: the record is deactivated (soft-deleted) and hidden from normal views, but retained in the database.
The global scope automatically filters to history = 1. This means you never see deactivated records unless you intentionally bypass the scope.
When you click Delete on a record, the system sets history = 0. The record is preserved for audit/Historical reference.

When writing custom queries with withoutGlobalScopes(), you MUST manually re-add: ->where('history', 1) and ->where('tenant_id', $tid). Forgetting this causes records from all tenants and all history states to appear.
The Admin > Audit Log page shows the complete change history across the system - every create, update, and soft-delete is logged with timestamp and user.

blocks.text: 1.3 Authentication and Authorization
SITHEHR uses JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication. Here is exactly how it works:

items: When you log in at /login, the server validates your email/password and issues a JWT token.
The JWT token is stored in an HTTP-only cookie named 'jwt_token'. HTTP-only means JavaScript cannot read it - this prevents XSS token theft.
The JwtMiddleware intercepts every request in the web group. It reads the cookie, validates the token, and attaches the user data to the request.
If the token is missing or expired, you are redirected to /login. Your session 'expires' - unsaved form data may be lost.
Every route has a permission requirement. Example: Route::get('/lab/tests', ...)->middleware('permission:lab.manage'). If your role lacks 'lab.manage' permission, you get a 403 Forbidden.
Permissions are assigned to roles (Admin > Roles > Role Permissions). Roles are assigned to users (Masters > Users or Admin > User Permissions).
Rate limiting: The /login route is throttled at 10 attempts per 1 minute (throttle:10,1). After too many failed attempts, wait 1 minute before trying again.
Logout clears the JWT cookie server-side. You return to /login.

blocks.text: 1.4 Permission System Reference
Every route requires a specific permission string. Here is the complete permission catalog with what each grants access to:

rows: Main dashboard at /dashboard - home/summary page with today's activity
All Masters menu items - country, region, province, city, barangay, religion, gender, civil-status, nationality, occupation, blood-type, relationship, hospital, permissions
Masters > Users - user CRUD, user list
General master data management umbrella permission
Admin > Role Permissions - assign permissions to roles
Admin > Audit Log - system-wide change history
Admin > Users > {userId}/permissions - override individual user permissions
All OPD pages: visit-types, consultation-types, referral-sources, services, clinics, complaints, consultations (OpdConsultationCrud)
ER master data: acuity-levels, mobility-statuses, zones, beds, area + admission EECL PDF
Admission (/admission), ICU (/icu), Ward (/ward), OR (/or), Transfers (/transfers) - all inpatient/admission related
Lab master data: sections, units, specimen-types, instruments, tests, panels, reference-ranges
Lab > Results - view and enter lab results, lab.result.print PDF
Radiology master data: modalities, body-parts, exam-types
Radiology > Results - view/enter radiology results, result.print PDF
Pharmacy master data: drugs, drug-batches, inventory, purchase-orders, stock-adjustments
Pharmacy > Dispensing - dispense medications to patients
Pharmacy > Patient Medication Record, pharmacy.request.print, pharmacy.request.encounter-print
Supply/CSR master data: units, categories, suppliers, stock-locations, items, inventory, stock-adjustments
Billing (/billing) - invoice management, patient accounts, payments, invoice/receipt/statement print
Billing > fund-sources, insurance-providers - master data for payment sources
PhilHealth > icd10-codes, rvs-codes, case-rates, hc-professionals, members
PhilHealth > claims, batches + all claim PDF routes (cf1pdf-cf5pdf, esoapdf, eeclpdf)
/settings - system settings, user profile, password change
/book-appointment - public appointment booking (NO LOGIN REQUIRED) - the only public route

blocks.text: 2. Getting Started: Login and Dashboard
This chapter covers the first things every user does.
2.1 Logging In
Navigate to http://localhost/login or click Login in the navigation. The login form has two fields:

items: Email address - your registered email (e.g. admin@demohospital.com)
Password - your password (e.g. Admin@12345 for the default admin)

blocks.text: On submit, the AuthLoginController@login (API route: POST api/auth/login) validates credentials and issues a JWT token stored in an HTTP-only cookie. You are redirected to /dashboard.
Default admin credentials for DEMO hospital: admin@demohospital.com / Admin@12345.
Rate limiting: The login route is throttled at 10 attempts per 1 minute. After too many failures, wait 1 minute before trying again.
2.2 The Dashboard
After login you land on /dashboard (route: dashboard, permission: dashboard.view, Livewire component: DashboardCrud). The dashboard shows:

items: Today's pending OPD consultations - patients waiting to be seen
Today's ER admissions - emergency patients currently in the ER
Pending lab/pharmacy/CSR/radiology/procedure requests awaiting action
Billing balances - outstanding patient balances
Quick-access cards linking to each major module
System-wide or tenant-scoped statistics depending on your role
Recent activity and alerts relevant to your permissions

blocks.text: The dashboard is the central navigation hub. From here you can jump to any module you have permission to access. The sidebar/top navigation shows the complete menu of accessible pages.

blocks.text: Pages you do not have permission for are hidden from the menu. Direct URL access without the required permission returns 403.
2.4 Logout

Click Logout in the navigation. The JWT cookie is cleared server-side and you return to /login. Save your work first - unsaved form data is lost on logout. If your session expires (JWT timeout), you are redirected to /login automatically.
